pr_title: lang/funcs: update cidrsubnet and cidrhost for 64-bit systems
pr_body:
The `cidrsubnet` and `cidrhost` functions were limited to supporting 32-bit systems. This PR:
* updates the `"github.com/apparentlymart/go-cidr"` library, which was recently extended with SubnetBig and HostBig functions
* switches to the new go-cidr functions, including passing appropriate values as `big.Int`s
* modifies terraform's validation check in `cidrsubnet` to check for bits > 64 instead of 32

Fixes  #25360

There's a new test, but for good measure, have some `terraform console` output:
```
> cidrsubnet("fe08::/64", 63, 0)
fe08::/127
```

issue_context.title: cidrsubnet doesn't work with ipv6  subnets
issue_context.body:

### Terraform Version

```
Terraform v0.12.3
+ provider.packet v2.9.0

Your version of Terraform is out of date! The latest version
is 0.12.26. You can update by downloading from www.terraform.io/downloads.html

```

### Terraform Configuration Files
<!--
Paste the relevant parts of your Terraform configuration between the ``` marks below.

For large Terraform configs, please use a service like Dropbox and share a link to the ZIP file. For security, you can also encrypt the files using our GPG public key.
-->

```hcl
locals {
service_cidr_range = cidrsubnet("fe08::/64", 63, 0)
}
```


### Expected Behavior
https://www.terraform.io/docs/configuration/functions/cidrsubnet.html documents `cidrsubnet` works for ipv6. and subnet sizes can go upto `128`.  So expected output here is
```
service_cidr_range => "fe08::/127"
```

### Actual Behavior
```

Error: Error in function call

  on provision.tf line 46, in locals:
  46:   service_cidr_range = cidrsubnet("fe08::/64", 63, 0)

Call to function "cidrsubnet" failed: may not extend prefix by more than 32
bits.
```

### Steps to Reproduce
```
terraform apply
```
### Additional Context
none

### References
none
comments:
Hi @arianvp!

I think what you are seeing here is a limitation that was addressed in Terraform v0.12.9: prior to that, Terraform was using 32-bit integer arithmetic internally to calculate the new bits to add, but from v0.12.9 onwards it uses an arbitrary-sized "big integer" implementation.

Could you please give this a try in Terraform 0.12.9 or later and let me know if you still see the problem? Thanks!
Just tested on `12.26` but same error

```

Error: Error in function call

  on provision.tf line 61, in locals:
  61:   service_cidr_range = cidrsubnet(cidrsubnet(data.packet_precreated_ip_block.addresses.cidr_notation,8,2),44,0)
    |----------------
    | data.packet_precreated_ip_block.addresses.cidr_notation is "2604:1380:2000:9d00::/56"

Call to function "cidrsubnet" failed: may not extend prefix by more than 32
```
Current workaround is to split up `cidrsubnet` in chunks of `/32` which is rather ugly :)

```
  service_cidr_range = cidrsubnet(cidrsubnet(cidrsubnet(data.packet_precreated_ip_block.addresses.cidr_notation,8,2),32,0),12,0)
```
Thanks for confirming, @arianvp! Looks like that old fix wasn't as complete as I thought it was. Indeed, now I look again at 
apparentlymart/go-cidr#16 I see that it was focused on the functionality that Terraform's `cidrhost` function depends on, and didn't change the `Subnet` function.

Re-reading that PR, I also remember why: the underlying library's `Subnet` function has the `num` argument typed as `int`, which is a 32-bit integer on 32-bit systems. That's part of the function's public interface, and so it can't be changed without a breaking change to the library. However, the `Subnet` function could potentially be paired with a new function `SubnetBig` that is typed `*big.Int` instead of `int`, and then it would be able to accept integers of any size that could fit inside an IPv6 address. It seems like `Host` could also benefit from having a corresponding `HostBig` for the same reason: the PR has ensured that `Host` will always calculate the result correctly on 32-bit systems, but it still can't produce a host address with the host portion greater than the current platform's `int`.

I reproduced what you saw on my system here, using a slightly modified configuration just because it's more convenient to use `output` blocks for cases like this, so we can easily see the final value once the bug is fixed:

```hcl
output "cidr_subnet" {
  value = cidrsubnet("fe08::/64", 63, 0)
}
```

```
Error: Error in function call

  on cidrsubnet-ipv6.tf line 2, in output "cidr_subnet":
   2:   value = cidrsubnet("fe08::/64", 63, 0)

Call to function "cidrsubnet" failed: may not extend prefix by more than 32
bits.
```

The error message is actually in Terraform itself: Terraform is converting from the Terraform language representation of numbers -- essentially a wrapped `big.Float` -- into an `int` to pass to the function, and so it encounters the range error when doing so. Once the upstream library has these new functions and we update Terraform to use those instead, we can change that validation rule to require that the value is a whole number, and let the underlying `cidr` library detect if the number is too big to fit in `newBits` bits.

If you have found a problem that seems similar to this, please open a new issue and complete the issue template so we can capture all the details necessary to investigate further.

review_comments:
I had honestly completely forgotten that `gocty` knows how to decode into `big.Int`! I'm glad to remember now that it does, cause I was originally expecting this change to be a bit more invasive.

One thing I notice looking back at the test cases for these functions is that they aren't testing the situation where the `newbits`, `hostnum`, `netnum` arguments are fractional numbers. I'm expecting that all of those would be properly rejected as invalid by the `gocty` conversions here (it should say something like "value must be a whole number") but might be worth adding some "expected error" test cases as insurance to future changes that might inadvertently make those panic otherwise.
